sahneler.metin: Eleven workers died when this oil rig exploded.
Then the well burst open, gushing oil for 87 days.
It became the largest marine oil spill in history.
But the disaster began with a test result nobody believed.
A pressure test showed gas leaking past the cement seal.
Why? The crew misread it as fine and kept going.
When the blowout came, the preventer couldn't cut the bent drill pipe.
One bad reading, and one valve that couldn't close.

aciklama:
On April 20, 2010, a blowout destroyed the Deepwater Horizon rig and killed 11 workers. A misread pressure test and a blowout preventer that could not seal the well turned it into the largest marine oil spill in history.
